X.note: The weathered plaster, exposed stonework, rubble, barrels and warm raking light look convincing and give real depth. The soldiers are flat, stiff, paper-cutout figures that don't match that realism, and the pose is repeated. The lane is more of a 3D render than a photo. Shutters and window openings are plausible for Gibraltar. The pole-mounted Union Jack is a bit off for the date.

Y.note: The walls are clean, smooth, saturated blue slabs with no texture or wear, so they look like a game or CAD mockup. The street is uniform gravel with sharp kerbs. The same stiff cutout soldiers look more toy-like here because nothing around them is weathered. The overall scene is much emptier and more modern-looking than X.

why: X has believable weathered materials, rubble, barrels and dramatic light that give a lived-in 1782 feel, while Y's untextured blue walls and clean ground look like a placeholder render.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the smooth blue wall shader with weathered lime-plaster and stone textures (cracks, stains, exposed masonry), recolour to warm limestone and ochre, and add rubble, debris and a dirt or cobble street; then replace the flat soldier sprites with properly modelled figures in varied poses.
anachronisms_seen: Pole-mounted Union Jack with 1801-style crosses/proportions (the 1782 flag would lack St Patrick's cross)
Clean uniform modern-looking stucco walls and kerbed street (Y)
Flat cutout soldiers with uniform tricorne/hat styling and a repeated pose
Large barrels and shutters that look more modern/generic than 18th-century
